vocabulary.en: an election in which voters choose candidates for a later election
vocabulary.excerpt: Michigan's primary shines a light on the deep divide in the Democratic Party
vocabulary.example_cn: 密歇根州的初选揭示了民主党内部的深刻分歧。

vocabulary.en: a difference or separation between two groups
vocabulary.excerpt: the deep divide in the Democratic Party
vocabulary.example_cn: 民主党内部的深刻分歧。

vocabulary.en: a set of beliefs or principles, especially one on which a political system is based
vocabulary.excerpt: whether voters are choosing an ideology or candidate they think can win in November
vocabulary.example_cn: 选民是在选择一种意识形态，还是选择他们认为能在十一月获胜的候选人。

vocabulary.en: the crime of deliberately setting fire to property
vocabulary.excerpt: a man is arrested on arson charges
vocabulary.example_cn: 一名男子因纵火罪被捕。

vocabulary.en: an amount of money paid as a guarantee that someone will return to court
vocabulary.excerpt: being held on a $1 million bond
vocabulary.example_cn: 被以100万美元保释金拘留。

vocabulary.en: the act of officially suggesting someone for a position or job
vocabulary.excerpt: the Senate Judiciary Committee will vote on Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general
vocabulary.example_cn: 参议院司法委员会将对托德·布兰奇担任司法部长的提名进行投票。

vocabulary.en: to officially end a law, decision, or agreement
vocabulary.excerpt: after Blanche formally rescinded the president's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
vocabulary.example_cn: 在布兰奇正式撤销总统的18亿美元反武器化基金之后。

vocabulary.en: relating to a state governor
vocabulary.excerpt: gubernatorial races
vocabulary.example_cn: 州长竞选。

vocabulary.en: dealing with problems in a practical and sensible way
vocabulary.excerpt: framing herself as the pragmatic choice
vocabulary.example_cn: 将自己定位为务实的选择。

vocabulary.en: a person who supports social and political change
vocabulary.excerpt: rallied Detroit progressives
vocabulary.example_cn: 召集了底特律的进步派人士。

vocabulary.en: public support for someone or something
vocabulary.excerpt: put up their endorsements
vocabulary.example_cn: 公开表示支持。

vocabulary.en: having a strong personal charm that attracts and influences people
vocabulary.excerpt: he's just extremely charismatic
vocabulary.example_cn: 他非常有魅力。

vocabulary.en: all the people who are allowed to vote in an election
vocabulary.excerpt: the electorate is actually pretty close
vocabulary.example_cn: 选民实际上相当接近。

vocabulary.en: the quality of being likely to win an election
vocabulary.excerpt: It comes down to that dreaded word electability.
vocabulary.example_cn: 这归结为那个可怕的字眼：可选举性。

vocabulary.en: relating to a political approach that claims to represent ordinary people
vocabulary.excerpt: The populist appeal that he has is really considerable.
vocabulary.example_cn: 他的民粹主义号召力相当可观。

vocabulary.en: a person's financial resources
vocabulary.excerpt: it's all pocketbook economic issues
vocabulary.example_cn: 都是与经济相关的问题。

vocabulary.en: to force someone to accept something they do not want
vocabulary.excerpt: those issues can be pretty much foisted on you
vocabulary.example_cn: 这些问题可能会强加于你。

vocabulary.en: to start a fire or to cause something to start
vocabulary.excerpt: He can ignite a populist fire.
vocabulary.example_cn: 他能点燃民粹主义的火焰。

vocabulary.en: a quality that makes someone admired or respected
vocabulary.excerpt: nobody else in the race at this time that has that cache
vocabulary.example_cn: 目前竞选中没有其他人拥有那种声望。

vocabulary.en: an unpredictable factor
vocabulary.excerpt: Is that the kind of thing that's a wild card here in Michigan?
vocabulary.example_cn: 这是密歇根州的一个变数吗？

vocabulary.en: the number of people who vote in an election
vocabulary.excerpt: to try to run up turnout in Black majority areas
vocabulary.example_cn: 试图提高黑人占多数地区的投票率。

vocabulary.en: an official expression of strong disapproval
vocabulary.excerpt: a Republican lawmaker facing censure
vocabulary.example_cn: 一名面临谴责的共和党议员。

vocabulary.en: moral principles that govern a person's behavior
vocabulary.excerpt: an ethics report
vocabulary.example_cn: 一份道德报告。

vocabulary.en: a court order that prevents someone from doing something
vocabulary.excerpt: filed for a temporary restraining order against Miller
vocabulary.example_cn: 申请对米勒的临时限制令。

vocabulary.en: a legal contract that prohibits sharing confidential information
vocabulary.excerpt: breaking the terms of a nondisclosure agreement
vocabulary.example_cn: 违反保密协议条款。

vocabulary.en: to criticize someone in a way that shows you do not respect them
vocabulary.excerpt: agreed not to disparage each other publicly
vocabulary.example_cn: 同意不公开诋毁对方。

vocabulary.en: a statement that someone has done something wrong, made without proof
vocabulary.excerpt: abuse allegations
vocabulary.example_cn: 虐待指控。

vocabulary.en: the state of being famous for something bad
vocabulary.excerpt: somebody trying to get notoriety
vocabulary.example_cn: 有人试图出名。

vocabulary.en: the legal right to take care of a child
vocabulary.excerpt: every minute he has custody of my granddaughter
vocabulary.example_cn: 他监护我孙女的每一分钟。

vocabulary.en: criticizing someone very severely
vocabulary.excerpt: released that scathing post on X
vocabulary.example_cn: 在X上发布了尖刻的帖子。

vocabulary.en: a person who works in the construction industry with steel
vocabulary.excerpt: he's running against an ironworker
vocabulary.example_cn: 他的对手是一名钢铁工人。

vocabulary.en: careful examination
vocabulary.excerpt: facing ethics scrutiny
vocabulary.example_cn: 面临道德审查。

vocabulary.en: large in amount and impressive
vocabulary.excerpt: lavish gifts
vocabulary.example_cn: 奢华的礼物。

vocabulary.en: the legal requirement that the state must respect all legal rights
vocabulary.excerpt: they've expressed some issues with due process
vocabulary.example_cn: 他们对正当程序提出了一些问题。

vocabulary.en: an action that is too extreme in response to a problem
vocabulary.excerpt: maybe a little bit of an overcorrection
vocabulary.example_cn: 可能有点过度纠正。

vocabulary.en: a limit on the amount of money a team can spend on players
vocabulary.excerpt: Major League Baseball salary cap
vocabulary.example_cn: 美国职业棒球大联盟的工资上限。

vocabulary.en: small and not important; in politics, a marginal seat is one that may be won by a small margin
vocabulary.excerpt: up in marginal seats
vocabulary.example_cn: 在边缘席位中。

vocabulary.en: a hypothetical set of multiple universes
vocabulary.excerpt: not like aliens from other dimensions coming in and messing up timelines
vocabulary.example_cn: 不像来自其他维度的外星人扰乱时间线。

sentences.en: Michigan's primary shines a light on the deep divide in the Democratic Party and ask whether voters are choosing an ideology or candidate they think can win in November.
sentences.cn: 密歇根州的初选揭示了民主党内部的深刻分歧，并询问选民是在选择一种意识形态，还是选择他们认为能在十一月获胜的候选人。
sentences.structure: 主语（Michigan's primary）+ 谓语（shines a light on）+ 宾语（the deep divide）+ 并列谓语（and ask）+ 宾语从句（whether...）
sentences.analysis: 该句为并列句，第一个分句用短语'shines a light on'表示揭示，第二个分句用'ask'后接whether引导的宾语从句，从句中'choosing'后接两个并列宾语'ideology'和'candidate'，'candidate'后接定语从句'they think can win'。

sentences.en: It's a key test of where the party is headed.
sentences.cn: 这是对党未来走向的关键考验。
sentences.structure: 主语（It）+ 系动词（is）+ 表语（a key test）+ 介词短语（of where...）
sentences.analysis: 表语后接of介词短语，其中where引导名词性从句作of的宾语，表示'党走向何方'。

sentences.en: There's Haley Stevens making her final campaign pitch, framing herself as the pragmatic choice to take on Republican Mike Rogers in November.
sentences.cn: 海利·史蒂文斯正在进行最后的竞选宣传，将自己定位为十一月对抗共和党人迈克·罗杰斯的务实选择。
sentences.structure: There be 句型 + 现在分词短语（making...）作后置定语，其中包含另一个现在分词短语（framing...）作伴随状语
sentences.analysis: There be句型中，主语后接现在分词短语作定语，'framing herself as'是伴随状语，表示'将自己定位为'。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Abdul El-Sayed rallied Detroit progressives and mounted a direct challenge to the party's Washington establishment.
sentences.cn: 与此同时，阿卜杜勒·埃尔-萨耶德召集了底特律的进步派人士，对党的华盛顿建制派发起了直接挑战。
sentences.structure: 主语（Abdul El-Sayed）+ 并列谓语（rallied... and mounted...）
sentences.analysis: 两个并列谓语动词，'rallied'表示召集，'mounted a challenge to'表示发起挑战。

sentences.en: I believe in the opportunity we have in front of us to take our democracy back from the likes of the corporations and the billionaires and the special interests who want to tell us what we cannot have and should not fight for.
sentences.cn: 我相信我们面前的机会，将我们的民主从那些公司、亿万富翁和特殊利益集团手中夺回来，他们想告诉我们什么我们不能拥有，也不应该为之奋斗。
sentences.structure: 主句（I believe in the opportunity）+ 定语从句（we have...）+ 不定式短语（to take...）作目的状语，其中包含定语从句（who want...）修饰special interests
sentences.analysis: 该句结构复杂，'opportunity'后接定语从句'we have in front of us'，不定式短语表示目的，'from the likes of'后接三个并列名词，'who'引导定语从句修饰'special interests'，从句中'what'引导宾语从句。

sentences.en: West Michigan needs a senator who's going to deliver, who's going to show up, who's going to show you that I can campaign like I govern and I govern like I campaign, I'm present, I'm focused, I'm dedicated.
sentences.cn: 西密歇根需要一位能够兑现承诺、能够挺身而出、能够向你展示我像治理一样竞选、像竞选一样治理的参议员，我在场，我专注，我投入。
sentences.structure: 主句（West Michigan needs a senator）+ 三个并列定语从句（who's going to...）+ 宾语从句（that I can...）
sentences.analysis: 三个who引导的定语从句并列修饰senator，第三个定语从句中嵌套that引导的宾语从句，宾语从句中又包含两个并列分句，最后三个短句强调个人品质。

sentences.en: Since we have such a clear division between the folks who have lined up behind Abdul El-Sayed, progressives, AOC, Bernie Sanders and so on.
sentences.cn: 因为我们之间存在着如此明显的分歧，一边是支持阿卜杜勒·埃尔-萨耶德、进步派、AOC、伯尼·桑德斯等人。
sentences.structure: 原因状语从句（Since...）+ 主句（we have...）+ 定语从句（who have lined up...）
sentences.analysis: Since引导原因状语从句，主句为'we have such a clear division'，'between'后接两个并列名词短语，第一个名词短语后接who引导的定语从句。

sentences.en: And beyond that, you have very clear ideological divides when it comes to Israel, which, you know, in our post-October 7th environment has become such a huge dividing line among Democrats as they look to build the future of their party.
sentences.cn: 除此之外，在以色列问题上存在非常明显的意识形态分歧，你知道，在我们10月7日后的环境中，这已成为民主党内部一条巨大的分界线，因为他们希望建设党的未来。
sentences.structure: 主句（you have...）+ 时间状语从句（when it comes to...）+ 非限制性定语从句（which...has become...）+ 原因状语从句（as they look...）
sentences.analysis: 主句为'you have very clear ideological divides'，'when it comes to'表示'当涉及'，which引导非限制性定语从句修饰'Israel'，从句中插入'you know'，最后as引导原因状语从句。

sentences.en: And for all the talk of divisions within the Democratic Party, the electorate is actually pretty close.
sentences.cn: 尽管民主党内部存在种种分歧的说法，但选民实际上相当接近。
sentences.structure: 让步状语（for all the talk...）+ 主句（the electorate is...）
sentences.analysis: 'for all'表示'尽管'，引导让步状语，主句说明选民实际状况。

sentences.en: So, yeah, there's this huge divide they have on Israel, but the whole party is moving in El-Sayed direction on Israel.
sentences.cn: 所以，是的，他们在以色列问题上存在巨大分歧，但整个政党在以色列问题上正朝着埃尔-萨耶德的方向前进。
sentences.structure: 并列句（there's... but...）
sentences.analysis: 两个分句由but连接，第一个分句为there be句型，第二个分句用现在进行时表示趋势。

sentences.en: The question of can I win in November is, is a question that voters alone can answer.
sentences.cn: 我能否在十一月获胜的问题，是只有选民才能回答的问题。
sentences.structure: 主语（The question of can I win in November）+ 系动词（is）+ 表语（a question）+ 定语从句（that voters alone can answer）
sentences.analysis: 主语中包含of介词短语，其中'can I win'为疑问句作宾语，表语后接that引导的定语从句。

sentences.en: Electability is the thing that's best defined after the fact.
sentences.cn: 可选举性是在事后才能最好定义的东西。
sentences.structure: 主语（Electability）+ 系动词（is）+ 表语（the thing）+ 定语从句（that's best defined...）
sentences.analysis: 定语从句修饰'the thing'，'after the fact'表示'事后'。

sentences.en: And so, I'm wondering if we're at the beginning of a movement that ends with some version of that for Democrats, someone that they thought was not electable, who suddenly is.
sentences.cn: 所以，我在想我们是否正处于一场运动的开端，这场运动最终会以某种形式出现在民主党人身上，一个他们曾认为没有当选可能的人，突然变得有当选可能。
sentences.structure: 主句（I'm wondering）+ 宾语从句（if we're...）+ 定语从句（that ends...）+ 同位语（someone）+ 定语从句（that they thought...）+ 非限制性定语从句（who suddenly is）
sentences.analysis: if引导宾语从句，'that ends with'修饰movement，'someone'是'that'的同位语，后接两个定语从句，第二个定语从句中省略了'electable'。

sentences.en: The conventional wisdom is Mike Rogers is very delighted to have El-Sayed as his opponent, but it's not entirely clear that that's the case.
sentences.cn: 传统观点认为，迈克·罗杰斯非常高兴有埃尔-萨耶德作为对手，但情况是否如此并不完全清楚。
sentences.structure: 并列句（The conventional wisdom is... but...）
sentences.analysis: 第一个分句中，'is'后接表语从句，第二个分句用it作形式主语，that从句为真正主语。

sentences.en: She's the only one in the race that's actually been elected.
sentences.cn: 她是竞选中唯一真正当选过的人。
sentences.structure: 主句（She's the only one）+ 定语从句（that's actually been elected）
sentences.analysis: 定语从句修饰'the only one'，'that'在从句中作主语。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, there's nobody else in the race at this time that has that cache.
sentences.cn: 不幸的是，目前竞选中没有其他人拥有那种声望。
sentences.structure: There be句型 + 定语从句（that has that cache）
sentences.analysis: 定语从句修饰'nobody else'，'that'在从句中作主语。

sentences.en: The strategy that the Stevens campaign is running is to try to run up turnout in Black majority areas in Michigan.
sentences.cn: 史蒂文斯竞选团队正在执行的策略是试图提高密歇根州黑人占多数地区的投票率。
sentences.structure: 主语（The strategy）+ 定语从句（that the Stevens campaign is running）+ 系动词（is）+ 表语（to try to run up...）
sentences.analysis: 定语从句修饰strategy，表语为不定式短语。

sentences.en: And the polling shows him ahead, but it's just sort of a guess by the pollsters about is it going to be young male white voters? Is it going to be older female black voters?
sentences.cn: 民调显示他领先，但这只是民调专家的一种猜测，会是年轻的白人男性选民吗？会是年长的黑人女性选民吗？
sentences.structure: 并列句（the polling shows... but...）+ 介词短语（about...）
sentences.analysis: 第一个分句为简单句，第二个分句'it's just sort of a guess'，后接about介词短语，其中包含两个疑问句作宾语。

sentences.en: President Trump publicly standing by embattled Republican Congressman Max Miller, even as his former press secretary launches a new legal battle against Miller.
sentences.cn: 特朗普总统公开支持陷入困境的共和党众议员马克斯·米勒，尽管他的前新闻秘书对米勒发起了新的法律诉讼。
sentences.structure: 独立主格结构（President Trump publicly standing by...）+ 让步状语从句（even as...）
sentences.analysis: 独立主格结构由名词+现在分词构成，表示伴随情况，'even as'引导让步状语从句。

sentences.en: In a "Washington Post" op-ed, Grisham had written about abuse allegations dealing with an ex-boyfriend, and Miller sued her at the time, but they settled out of court and agreed not to disparage each other publicly.
sentences.cn: 在《华盛顿邮报》的一篇专栏文章中，格里沙姆曾写过关于前男友的虐待指控，米勒当时起诉了她，但他们庭外和解，并同意不公开诋毁对方。
sentences.structure: 并列句（Grisham had written... and Miller sued... but they settled...）
sentences.analysis: 三个分句由and和but连接，第一个分句为过去完成时，第二个分句为一般过去时，第三个分句为一般过去时。

sentences.en: What should be noted is that allegation came out on the same day as somebody's book launch.
sentences.cn: 值得注意的是，这一指控是在某人新书发布当天出现的。
sentences.structure: 主语从句（What should be noted）+ 系动词（is）+ 表语从句（that allegation came out...）
sentences.analysis: What引导主语从句，that引导表语从句，'the same day as'表示'与...同一天'。

sentences.en: And she, in her own words, will tell you that I never did any of those things.
sentences.cn: 而且她，用她自己的话说，会告诉你我从未做过那些事。
sentences.structure: 主语（she）+ 插入语（in her own words）+ 谓语（will tell）+ 间接宾语（you）+ 宾语从句（that I never did...）
sentences.analysis: 插入语' in her own words'表示'用她自己的话'，that引导宾语从句。

sentences.en: It appears this was a confidential agreement.
sentences.cn: 看来这是一份保密协议。
sentences.structure: 主语（It）+ 系动词（appears）+ 表语从句（this was...）
sentences.analysis: It作形式主语，appears后接表语从句。

sentences.en: And she's saying that in that interview, by denying the claims that she made, as well as the claims by his now ex-wife, that he broke that agreement.
sentences.cn: 她说，在那次采访中，通过否认她提出的指控以及他前妻的指控，他违反了该协议。
sentences.structure: 主句（she's saying）+ 宾语从句（that...he broke...）+ 方式状语（by denying...）
sentences.analysis: that引导宾语从句，'by denying'为方式状语，其中'that she made'为定语从句修饰claims，'as well as'连接并列宾语。

sentences.en: And there is also this audio obtained from earlier this year.
sentences.cn: 还有今年早些时候获得的这段音频。
sentences.structure: There be句型 + 过去分词短语（obtained...）作后置定语
sentences.analysis: 过去分词短语修饰audio。

sentences.en: Emily Moreno is telling police about an incident on New Year's Eve where she alleged that Miller held a gun to her head when she was changing their infant daughter.
sentences.cn: 艾米丽·莫雷诺正在向警方讲述新年夜发生的一起事件，她声称米勒在她给婴儿女儿换尿布时用枪指着她的头。
sentences.structure: 主句（Emily Moreno is telling police about an incident）+ 定语从句（where she alleged...）+ 时间状语从句（when she was changing...）
sentences.analysis: where引导定语从句修饰incident，从句中that引导宾语从句，宾语从句中又包含when引导的时间状语从句。

sentences.en: And I think that's part of the problem is that he keeps releasing more and more information and more evidence that can then be used against him in certain cases.
sentences.cn: 我认为部分问题在于他不断发布越来越多的信息和证据，这些信息和证据在特定情况下可能会对他不利。
sentences.structure: 主句（I think）+ 宾语从句（that's part of the problem）+ 表语从句（that he keeps...）+ 定语从句（that can then be used...）
sentences.analysis: 第一个that引导宾语从句，第二个that引导表语从句，第三个that引导定语从句修饰evidence。

sentences.en: Bernie Moreno didn't say anything for a very long time.
sentences.cn: 伯尼·莫雷诺在很长一段时间内没有说任何话。
sentences.structure: 主语（Bernie Moreno）+ 谓语（didn't say）+ 宾语（anything）+ 时间状语（for a very long time）
sentences.analysis: 简单句，否定形式。

sentences.en: I hope you never have to go through a situation like this and you wouldn't ask that kind of effing question.
sentences.cn: 我希望你永远不必经历这样的情况，你也不会问那种该死的问题。

But it's just another thing that stacks up.

JESSE ARM, POLLSTER: Well, that's the key point. I don't think any undecided voters are going to be making their decision based on reflecting pool dynamics.

AUDIE CORNISH, CNN ANCHOR: Got it. Okay.

Straight ahead on CNN THIS MORNING, Michigan's primary shines a light on the deep divide in the Democratic Party and ask whether voters are choosing an ideology or candidate they think can win in November. Plus, crews scrambling to gain control on wildfires in Washington state as the weather turns dangerous again.

CORNISH: Good morning, everybody. I'm Audie Cornish. Thank you for joining me on CNN THIS MORNING.

It is half past the hour. And here's what's happening right now.

In Washington, a man is arrested on arson charges in connection with one of three wildfires burning in the state. The 37-year-old man is being held on a $1 million bond, and officials say the fires are expected to keep burning for weeks. Already, more than 65,000 people have been forced from their homes.

And in just a few hours, the Senate Judiciary Committee will vote on Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general. The first vote was delayed last week due to concerns from two key Republicans, but both have signaled they will vote yes after Blanche formally rescinded the presidents $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund.

And happening now, polls are set to open for critical primary elections in five key states. Michigan, Missouri, Kansas, Virginia and Washington. Today's races will settle nominations in the Senate, House and gubernatorial races as we get closer to the midterms this November.

And one of today's most closely watched contests is Michigan's Democratic Senate primary. It's a key test of where the party is headed. There's Haley Stevens making her final campaign pitch, framing herself as the pragmatic choice to take on Republican Mike Rogers in November.

Meanwhile, Abdul El-Sayed rallied Detroit progressives and mounted a direct challenge to the party's Washington establishment.

ABDUL EL-SAYED (D), MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE; I believe in what we're going to do. I believe in the opportunity we have in front of us to take our democracy back from the likes of the corporations and the billionaires and the special interests who want to tell us what we cannot have and should not fight for.

REP. HALEY STEVENS (D), MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE: West Michigan needs a senator who's going to deliver, who's going to show up, who's going to show you that I can campaign like I govern and I govern like I campaign, I'm present, I'm focused, I'm dedicated.

CORNISH: Joining me now, two journalists who have been following these candidates closely. Dana Milbank, political columnist for "NOTUS", and Nicholas Wu, congressional reporter for "Semafor".

Let me start with my congressional reporter. I know you like to cover the House, so it must be so irritating to be stuck covering the Senate. What is it about this race that you think is making it kind of one of the most written about?

NICHOLAS WU, CONGRESSIONAL REPORTER, SEMAFOR: Well, this is one of the clearest ideological divides were seeing in pretty much any Senate race in the country in the primary. Since we have such a clear division between the folks who have lined up behind Abdul El-Sayed, progressives, AOC, Bernie Sanders and so on.

CORNISH: And put up their endorsements so people can see that pretty clearly. Haley stevens got Chuck Schumer, Gretchen Whitmer. It is -- it's pretty obvious if you were drawing, if you asked a kid to draw a picture of wings of the party, these are the faces that would be on opposite sides.

WU: Exactly. And beyond that, you have very clear ideological divides when it comes to Israel, which, you know, in our post-October 7th environment has become such a huge dividing line among Democrats as they look to build the future of their party.

CORNISH: How come you say this is not a civil war? You've been writing about this, and it sounds like you think it's overblown. DANA MILBANK, POLITICAL COLUMNIST, NOTUS: I mean, what Nick is saying

is all true. I think some of it is a little overblown. I mean, one of the main reasons El-Sayed is doing so well is he's just extremely charismatic. I mean, he's a very good politician, you know?

And for all the talk of divisions within the Democratic Party, the electorate is actually pretty close. You know, it's probably more unified than it's been really in decades. And you see, you know, even the mainstream of the party, the so-called establishment, has gone substantially to the left in recent years. So, yeah, there's this huge divide they have on Israel, but the whole party is moving in El-Sayed direction on Israel.

They're both looking for universal health care, just different ways of getting there.

MILBANK: So a lot of --

CORNISH: It comes down to that dreaded word electability. Here's what Abdul El-Sayed said about that when he was asked on CNN on Sunday.

JEFF ZELENY, CNN CHIEF NATIONAL AFFAIRS CORRESPONDENT: How much of this is about convincing people that you can win in November?

EL-SAYED: The question of can I win in November is, is a question that voters alone can answer. Convincing folks like you and everybody who watches from everywhere else, I'm so sorry. It just doesn't matter.

Electability is the thing that's best defined after the fact. So -- if and when I get elected, then you'll know I'm electable.

CORNISH: I feel like Donald Trump, it applied to him, right? Like for the longest time, all I heard from Republicans is this guy is not a Republican. This isn't serious. Some of the people in his cabinet, some of the people who are with him now were people who said he was not electable. And here we are.

And so, I'm wondering if we're at the beginning of a movement that ends with some version of that for Democrats, someone that they thought was not electable, who suddenly is.

MILBANK: Yeah, I'm not sure that he's wrong in making this electability argument. The populist appeal that he has is really considerable. You know, you don't hear a word out of his mouth about sort of the woke issues, the cultural issues, and it's all pocketbook economic issues. So I'm sure --

CORNISH: But I think those issues can be pretty much foisted on you when you get to a general election, right? Like everything that Mamdani is doing in New York becomes the thing that everyone else has to run against.

MILBANK: Right. I mean, the conventional wisdom is Mike Rogers is very delighted to have El-Sayed as his opponent, but it's not entirely clear that that's the case.

MILBANK: He can ignite a populist fire. And that's what will be interesting in the fall.

CORNISH: Let me play one more thing for you. It's the vote I always keep an eye on in states like this. This is the Reverend Dr. Charles William II on CNN. This was on Sunday.

REV. DR. CHARLES WILLIAMS II, SENIOR PASTOR, HISTORIC KING SOLOMON BAPTIST CHURCH: She's the only one in the race that's actually been elected. She was elected a congressperson. She worked in the executive branch.

And of course, she has been a legislator. She understands how to work to get policy passed. Unfortunately, there's nobody else in the race at this time that has that cache.

CORNISH: Historic King Solomon Church. There is always that Black Church vote that comes out, and they aren't always aligned with the academic progressive left vote. We see this in South Carolina. Biden was happy to receive those votes.

Is that the kind of thing that's a wild card here in Michigan, or are those voters also embracing some of these more populist ideas or ideas on foreign policy?

WU: I mean, the strategy that the Stevens campaign is running is to try to run up turnout in Black majority areas in Michigan. Whether that is --

CORNISH: I think I saw her at a church.

WU: Exactly. Right. Right.

CORNISH: The obligatory many times Democrats, Black church visit. That happens.

WU: Exactly. She's been trying to run up turnout there. El-Sayed has been trying to cut into those margins. For example, you know, we saw him going around Detroit with a whole crew of influencers. So it's like it's a much different kind of strategy --

CORNISH: Very different reach, but I understand.

WU: Exactly. MILBANK: And the polling shows him ahead, but it's just sort of a

guess by the pollsters about is it going to be young male white voters? Is it going to be older female black voters? We don't really know until tonight or tomorrow.

CORNISH: Yeah. Both are frustrated for different reasons. And there's always the couch, as it's said, right.

You guys, thank you so much. Hope to have you back in the group.

And tonight, don't miss key primary races across the country, including big gubernatorial and congressional races, as we've talked about of Michigan. We're going to talk about who's going to advance and we're going to have election results all night.

You can get that tonight on CNN and our CNN app.

DONALD TRUMP, PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES: I know Max. He's a -- he's a good person. I mean, I always thought he was a very good person. And I'm going to let the families figure that out. But it's accusations, and I'm going to let them figure that out.

CORNISH: President Trump publicly standing by embattled Republican Congressman Max Miller, even as his former press secretary launches a new legal battle against Miller.
